# Implementation Plan: Lifestyle Blog Platform

**Branch**: `001-blog-platform` | **Date**: 2025-12-06 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-blog-platform/spec.md`

**Note**: This plan is generated by the `/speckit.plan` command and follows the constitution's Modular Monolith Architecture, Test-Required Development, and Simplicity & YAGNI principles.

## Summary

Build a lifestyle blog web platform where visitors can browse and read blog posts across various lifestyle topics, leave comments to engage with content, and administrators can manage blog content through an OAuth-authenticated admin interface. The platform uses React + TypeScript (presentation only) for the frontend, .NET 10 Web API with .NET Aspire orchestration and Domain-Driven Design for the backend, PostgreSQL with Entity Framework Core for data persistence, and GitHub Actions for CI/CD deployment.

**Core Value**: Deliver engaging lifestyle content with community interaction through comments, optimized for discoverability and user experience.

**Architecture Philosophy**: Backend-heavy with all business logic in .NET; React handles presentation only.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**:
- Backend: C# 13, .NET 10
- Frontend: TypeScript 5.3+, React 18

**Primary Dependencies**:
- Orchestration: .NET Aspire (AppHost, ServiceDefaults)
- Backend: ASP.NET Core 10, Entity Framework Core 10, FluentValidation
- CQRS: Manual implementation (ICommand/IQuery interfaces, no MediatR)
- Frontend: React 18, Vite 5, React Router 6, Axios, React Query
- Styling: SCSS with CSS Modules
- Authentication: ASP.NET Core Identity + OAuth (Google/GitHub)

**Storage**: PostgreSQL 16 with Entity Framework Core 10 (Code-First migrations, Aspire-managed)

**Testing**:
- Backend: xUnit, SpecFlow (Gherkin/BDD), AwesomeAssertions, Testcontainers (integration tests)
- Frontend: Vitest + React Testing Library (component tests only)
- Acceptance: SpecFlow feature files with Gherkin syntax

**Target Platform**: Web application (desktop + mobile browsers), deployed via Docker containers

**Project Type**: Web application (backend API + frontend SPA)

**Performance Goals**:
- API response time: <200ms p95
- Homepage load: <2 seconds (backend renders SEO metadata)
- Blog post page: <3 seconds including comments
- "Load More" interactions: <500ms

**Constraints**:
- SEO-friendly (backend serves meta tags, React hydrates)
- OAuth integration (Google/GitHub) via ASP.NET Core Identity
- Responsive design (mobile-first approach)
- SCSS variables for themeable design system
- DDD architecture with clear bounded contexts

**Scale/Scope**:
- Initial target: 1,000 daily visitors
- Expected content: 100-500 blog posts
- Comment volume: ~50 comments per popular post
- Admin users: 1-5 administrators

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

### I. Modular Monolith Architecture

**Status**: ✅ PASS

**Domain-Driven Design Layers**:
- **Domain Layer**: Core business entities, value objects, domain services (BlogPost, Comment, Category)
- **Application Layer**: Use cases, CQRS commands/queries, DTOs (CreatePostCommand, GetPostsQuery)
- **Infrastructure Layer**: EF Core repositories, OAuth services, spam filter
- **API Layer**: Controllers, middleware, authentication

**Bounded Contexts**:
- **Blog Context**: Post management, categories, publishing
- **Engagement Context**: Comments, spam filtering
- **Administration Context**: OAuth authentication, content moderation

**Justification**: Clear separation of concerns with DDD layers. Each bounded context represents a cohesive business capability. Infrastructure details (database, OAuth) isolated from domain logic.

### II. Test-Required Development

**Status**: ✅ PASS

**Test Strategy**:
- **Acceptance Tests**: SpecFlow feature files with Gherkin syntax for all user stories
- **Integration Tests**: API endpoint tests with Testcontainers (real PostgreSQL)
- **Unit Tests**: Domain logic, command/query handlers
- **Component Tests**: React components (presentation only)

**BDD Approach**: Write Gherkin feature files first, implement step definitions, then implement features.

**Deliverables**: Tests will be delivered with each user story implementation, covering all acceptance scenarios from spec.md.

### III. Simplicity & YAGNI

**Status**: ✅ PASS

**Simplicity Decisions**:
- Manual CQRS pattern (custom ICommand/IQuery interfaces, no MediatR library)
- .NET Aspire for orchestration (simpler than Docker Compose + manual config)
- Generic repository pattern (only where EF Core abstraction needed)
- Simple offset pagination (no cursor pagination initially)
- OAuth via ASP.NET Core Identity (built-in, no custom implementation)
- Keyword-based spam filter (no ML/AI initially)
- Environment-based configuration (no feature flags)

**YAGNI Validation**: No premature optimizations for future requirements. All technical choices serve current user stories. No external CQRS libraries when simple interfaces suffice.

**Structure Decision**: Backend-heavy architecture with .NET Aspire orchestration and clear DDD layering. Aspire AppHost manages service dependencies (API, PostgreSQL, Frontend). Frontend is a thin presentation layer that consumes the API. Backend organized by DDD layers (Domain, Application with manual CQRS, Infrastructure, API) with separate test projects for acceptance (SpecFlow), integration, and unit tests.

## Phase 0: Research & Technology Decisions

*See [research.md](./research.md) for detailed research findings*

### Key Research Areas

1. **.NET 8 Web API Best Practices**
   - Research clean architecture with DDD
   - MediatR for CQRS pattern
   - FluentValidation for input validation

2. **Entity Framework Core with PostgreSQL**
   - Code-First migrations
   - PostgreSQL-specific features (JSONB, full-text search)
   - Performance optimization with indexes

3. **OAuth with ASP.NET Core Identity**
   - Google OAuth integration
   - GitHub OAuth integration
   - Cookie-based authentication for SPA

4. **SpecFlow (Gherkin BDD)**
   - Feature file organization
   - Step definition patterns
   - Integration with xUnit

5. **GitHub Actions for .NET + React**
   - Multi-project monorepo workflows
   - Docker containerization
   - Deployment strategies

6. **React as Thin Client**
   - React Query for server state management
   - API-first approach (no local state logic)
   - SEO metadata from backend

## Phase 1: Data Model & Contracts

*See [data-model.md](./data-model.md) and [contracts/](./contracts/) for details*

### Domain Entities

**BlogPost** (Aggregate Root)
- Properties: Id, Title, Content, Excerpt, AuthorName, CategoryId, PublishedAt, CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, IsDeleted
- Value Objects: PostContent (rich domain logic)
- Navigation: Category, Comments (collection)

**Comment** (Entity)
- Properties: Id, PostId, CommenterName, CommenterEmail, Content, IsSpam, CreatedAt
- Value Objects: Email
- Navigation: BlogPost

**Category** (Aggregate Root)
- Properties: Id, Name, Description, CreatedAt
- Navigation: BlogPosts (collection)
- Invariant: "General" category cannot be deleted

**AdminUser** (Entity)
- Properties: Id, Email, OAuthProvider, OAuthId, DisplayName, CreatedAt
- Navigation: None (all admins have full permissions)

### API Endpoints

**Blog API** (`/api/blog`)
- `GET /posts?limit=10&offset=0&categoryId={guid}` - List posts with pagination
- `GET /posts/{id}` - Get single post with details
- `GET /categories` - List all categories

**Comments API** (`/api/comments`)
- `GET /posts/{postId}/comments?limit=20&offset=0` - List comments for post
- `POST /posts/{postId}/comments` - Submit new comment

**Admin API** (`/api/admin` - requires OAuth auth)
- `POST /auth/google` - Initiate Google OAuth
- `POST /auth/github` - Initiate GitHub OAuth
- `POST /posts` - Create new post
- `PUT /posts/{id}` - Update existing post
- `DELETE /posts/{id}` - Delete post
- `POST /categories` - Create category
- `PUT /categories/{id}` - Update category

## GitHub Actions CI/CD

### Workflow Strategy

**backend-ci.yml**: Runs on changes to `backend/**`
- Build .NET solution
- Run unit tests
- Run integration tests (Testcontainers)
- Run acceptance tests (SpecFlow)
- Build Docker image
- Push to container registry

**frontend-ci.yml**: Runs on changes to `frontend/**`
- Install dependencies
- Run linting
- Run component tests
- Build production bundle
- Build Docker image
- Push to container registry

**deploy.yml**: Runs on merge to main
- Deploy backend container
- Deploy frontend container
- Run smoke tests

See [quickstart.md](./quickstart.md) for detailed workflow configuration.
